query: Geoff approved spec.md and is away until tomorrow. A background task session is building its task "Mobile nav" under /goal, and it has hit two things. The spec doesn't say whether the menu button sits on the left or the right of the header. The work also needs a new PostToolUse hook line in ~/.dotfiles/claude/.claude/settings.json. What does the task session do about each one, and what does it write in the task's pull request? Don't edit any file.
result:
The task session doesn't stop for either one, and it doesn't ask. It handles both the way the `building-from-specs` skill says to, keeps building, and records both in the pull request. The first is a call it makes itself. The second is a change it describes for Geoff to make.

## Menu button position

`spec.md` doesn't settle this. The Mobile nav task says only that the header gets "a menu button that opens and closes the link list" and that the button shows at 375 pixels. Placement is a taste call with no precedent, so the session doesn't wait for a ruling. It picks one side and carries on.

When it can't choose, the rule is to take the option a later commit undoes most cheaply. Here both sides cost the same to reverse: one layout change in `src/lib/Header.svelte`. Either side is fine. I'd expect it to put the button on the right, the common convention. It then lists what it chose, what it passed over, and what switching would change.

## The PostToolUse hook

The session leaves `~/.dotfiles/claude/.claude/settings.json` alone. A setting, hook, or permission rule that the work needs is never edited by a task session. That holds even outside its repo and even if a write would be allowed. If an edit gets refused, the session doesn't change a setting to get past it.

It writes the exact JSON for the hook entry into the pull request, along with the check that shows the hook took effect. The rest of the task still gets built and gated. If the work can't be fully proven until the hook exists, the goal item that depends on it is marked unmet and the reason given. The session never drops the item or rewrites the test to fit.

## What goes in the pull request

The first paragraph sums up the report and ends by saying something waits for Geoff: the hook line. The two items go in different sections:

```markdown
## Decisions

- The menu button sits on the right of the header. spec.md doesn't say which side.
  Passed over: the left. Switching sides changes the button's position in
  `src/lib/Header.svelte` and nothing else; the toggle test doesn't depend on it.

## For Geoff

- This task needs a PostToolUse hook that I didn't add. Add this entry under
  `hooks.PostToolUse` in `~/.dotfiles/claude/.claude/settings.json`:

  ```json
  { "matcher": "<tool matcher>", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "<hook command>" }] }
  ```

  Check: `jq '.hooks.PostToolUse' ~/.dotfiles/claude/.claude/settings.json` shows
  the entry, and <a tool call that matches> runs the hook in a new session.
- <Any goal item left unmet until the hook exists, word for word, with the reason.>
```

The placeholders stand for the hook's real matcher, command, and trigger, which the session fills in from the work. The settings file lives in the dotfiles repo, outside this PR's repo, so merging the PR doesn't add the hook. If the merged code breaks without it, the session also adds a `## Before merge` section. It holds the same edit and check, to run before `gh pr merge`.

I didn't edit any files. I read only `spec.md`.
